title: Bridge link v1: shared definitions
description: Definitions the frames of the Arkab bridge <-> Alnasl link share. The link is one WebSocket per server, dialled by the bridge. Every data frame in both directions is a JSON TEXT frame holding one object with a "type"; there are no binary data frames. The only other frames are WebSocket control frames: the bridge sends a ping with an EMPTY payload every 25 s and answers pings with pongs; a line silent for 75 s is dead. The bytes the bridge writes to a DGT board's serial line when it opens it are pinned in dgt-serial-opening.schema.json.

version.description: The protocol version. 1 is the only one.

board_id.description: A board's name on the link (Arkab.Protocol.board_id/2): its port, "COM3", or on a DGT loop "<port>#<bus address>", "/dev/ttyUSB0#12799". A played-back board is called whatever the bridge's source names it.

position.description: Arkab.Board.to_text/1: 64 characters, a8 first, then b8 ... h8, a7 ... h1. Upper case White, lower case Black, "." an empty square.

event.description: One driver event as it is queued and sent (Arkab.Protocol.encode_event/4).

s.description: The event's number in the bridge's queue. Only goes up, never reused, also across restarts.

t.description: When it happened, in milliseconds: the bridge's wall clock (Unix epoch ms) for a real board, the recording's own clock for a played-back one (then "at" is present too).

at.description: Only from a played-back board (Arkab.Driver.Player): [speed, next]. speed is the playback speed factor; next is the recording time (ms) of the following event, or null after the last.

event_fields.description: The driver event itself, "k" says which. Raw serial bytes ("rx"/"tx") are never sent on the link: they stay in the bridge's capture files.

event_position.description: The whole board as it stands now.

r.description: Whose time is running, or none.

l.description: The side the lever is set for (armed), when the clock says. Absent when unknown.

event_status.description: The board itself came or went (not the link).

event_poll_ok.description: The board answered. Answers are thinned to about one a second; "n" is how many answers this one stands for, absent when 1.

event_poll_missed.description: The board did not answer. Always sent, never thinned.

event_info.description: What a board says about itself. Only these names travel (Arkab.Protocol's list); each event carries the ones that changed, or on resend all that are known.

serial.description: The board's serial number, as the board says it ("06310").

battery.description: Bluetooth boards' battery message, upper-case hex of its data bytes.

bus_address.description: The DGT bus address the board answered a ping with; null when none answered.

error.description: Why the port could not be opened or read, as text.

loop.description: null: one board (or none) on this port. A list of two or more bus addresses: the port is a loop and is read as one.

loop_number.description: On a loop: the board's bus address.

clock.description: Only ever false: the clock was switched off or unplugged; its last reading is not to be believed.
